name: Autoimmune Pancreatitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Consensus Diagnostic Criteria (ICDC) for Autoimmune Pancreatitis 2011

criteria.description: Parenchymal imaging: diffuse enlargement with delayed enhancement (sausage-shaped pancreas), or focal/segmental enlargement
Ductal imaging: long (>1/3 length) or multiple strictures without upstream dilatation
Serology: elevated serum IgG4 >= 2x upper limit of normal (Type 1)
Other organ involvement (OOI): bile duct, retroperitoneal fibrosis, salivary/lacrimal gland, renal
Histology: lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with storiform fibrosis and obliterative phlebitis, >10 IgG4+ cells/HPF (Type 1)
Histology: granulocytic epithelial lesion (GEL) in pancreatic ducts (Type 2)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Combination of imaging, serology, other organ involvement, histology, and steroid response; classified as definite or probable Type 1 or Type 2 based on ICDC algorithm
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Type 1 is part of IgG4-related disease spectrum. Type 2 (IDCP) is associated with IBD (~20%), younger age, and GELs. Critical to distinguish from pancreatic cancer.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sausage-shaped diffusely enlarged pancreas on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Diffuse enlargement with loss of lobular contour and capsule-like rim; highly suggestive

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive jaundice without discrete mass with elevated IgG4
pathognomonic.notes: Mimics pancreatic cancer; distinguishing feature is response to steroids
searchTerms: jaundice without tumor and high IgG4

common.notes: Painless or mildly painful; from bile duct stricture
Often less severe than in regular pancreatitis

laboratory: Elevated serum IgG4 (>135 mg/dL; >2x ULN highly suggestive for Type 1)
Elevated serum bilirubin and ALP (biliary obstruction)
CA 19-9 mildly elevated (can overlap with pancreatic cancer levels)
Elevated serum lipase/amylase (less common than in alcoholic/gallstone pancreatitis)
imaging: CT/MRI: diffuse pancreatic enlargement (sausage-shaped) with delayed enhancement and capsule-like rim
MRCP/EUS: diffuse or focal pancreatic duct narrowing without upstream dilatation
PET-CT: FDG avid pancreas (must distinguish from cancer)
CT: bile duct wall thickening, renal lesions, retroperitoneal fibrosis
other: EUS-guided biopsy/FNA: lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis, increased IgG4+ plasma cells (Type 1); GEL (Type 2)
Steroid trial: rapid improvement in symptoms and imaging supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: AIP Type 1 is part of IgG4-RD spectrum

redFlags: Clinical presentation indistinguishable from pancreatic cancer (must exclude malignancy before steroid trial)
Failure to respond to steroids within 2 weeks (reconsider diagnosis)
Recurrence after steroid taper (common; may need maintenance immunosuppression)
references: Shimosegawa T, et al. International consensus diagnostic criteria for autoimmune pancreatitis: guidelines of the International Association of Pancreatology. Pancreas. 2011;40(3):352-358.
Hart PA, et al. Recent Advances in Autoimmune Pancreatitis. Gastroenterology. 2015;149(1):39-51.
Okazaki K, et al. International consensus for the treatment of autoimmune pancreatitis. Pancreatology. 2017;17(1):1-6.
